Rule Description: In an RME system, any access by a requester and any instruction executed by a PE is associated with a single Security state.
Notes: Broad architectural invariant; ACS validates observable access behavior in other tests.

Rule Description: Association of a Resource with a Resource PAS is controlled by either SSD or MSD.
Notes: Resource ownership control is SSD/MSD policy and implementation-specific.

Rule Description: Resource accesses carry an Access PAS and MECID as required by the architecture.
Requesters outside MMU/SMMU translation are SSD-tagged with an Access PAS.
Notes: Requires DAP/debug-access support to generate and tag non-MMU/SMMU requests.

Rule Description: Once assigned, the value of an Access PAS cannot be altered.
Notes: Access PAS tag mutation is internal behavior and not directly observable by ACS.

Rule Description: A PAS filter enforces the PAS protection check by permitting access to a Resource only if the Access PAS matches a Resource PAS associated with that Resource.
Every requester in the system is subjected to the PAS protection check.
Notes: PCIe exerciser VIP required

Rule Description: Access to the Root PAS is only permitted for Trusted requesters.
Notes: Trusted requester access policy is not generically observable by ACS.

Rule Description: GPT-based PAS assignment requires a single PA per PAS and page-granular resources.
On-chip Resource GPC relies only on GPT storage with equivalent integrity and replay protection.
Notes: GPT storage location, integrity, and replay protection are implementation details.

Rule Description: GPC-protected non-idempotent accesses are not speculatively performed before the check completes.
Notes: Non-idempotent speculation behavior is not directly software-observable.

Rule Description: If a requester-side Granular PAS filter is in reset state, any requester that is associated with it is either in reset state or blocked from accessing memory.
Notes: PCIe exerciser VIP required

Rule Description: A PA that targets memory that can be cached is associated with a PAS until reaching the PoPA.
Where a PA is associated with a PAS, any PA compare operation includes the PAS.
A PoPA CMO affects all cached copies for the specified {PAS, PA}, independent of shareability domain or MECID.
An access to a cacheable memory Location is associated with a MECID until reaching the PoE.
Notes: PCIe exerciser VIP required

Rule Description: Memory accesses resulting from a cache Clean operation, due to cache maintenance operations and natural evictions, use the MECID that the entry was cached with.
External Secure, Realm, and Root memory is encrypted with distinct contexts and address tweaks.
Notes: PCIe exerciser VIP required for mec_mecid_assosiation_and_encryption

Rule Description: Data is encrypted before being written to external memory or to any shared cache that resides past the PoPA.
Notes: PCIe exerciser VIP required

Rule Description: Memory-mapped data structures that store encryption contexts must reside in SMEM in the Root PAS, such as MSD SMEM.
Notes: MEC encryption-context storage is not generically discoverable by ACS.

Rule Description: ECC-scrubbing engines beyond PoPA must not leak confidential information.
Notes: ECC scrubber behavior depends on implementation-specific RAS logic.

Rule Description: A PA of an access to a memory-mapped peripheral is associated with a PAS until reaching the PAS filter assigned to protect the peripheral.
A private PAS filter allows access to a register only if the Access PAS matches a Resource PAS that the register is associated with.
Non-PE requesters use the permitted RME Security states.
Notes: Non-PE requester security-state behavior is implementation-specific.

Rule Description: A fully coherent non-PE requester that is not part of the System Security Domain (SSD) will not observe coherency traffic for addresses in the Secure, Realm, or Root PAS.
Notes: Generic ACS infrastructure does not support coherent-device traffic visibility.

Rule Description: Programmable all-PAS completer filters keep controls in Root PAS and reset safely.
Notes: Completer-side PAS filter controls are implementation-defined.

Rule Description: Secure/Non-secure completer filters keep controls in Secure or Root PAS and reset safely.
Notes: Completer-side PAS filter controls are implementation-defined.

Rule Description: TSM functionality in RME-DA is implemented within RMSD.
Notes: TSM/RMM software presence is outside hardware ACS scope.

Rule Description: Realm-assigned TDI translated accesses are subject to DPT checks unless exempted.
Coverage: dpt_p2p_different_rootport_invalid, dpt_p2p_different_rootport_valid, dpt_p2p_same_rootport_invalid, dpt_p2p_same_rootport_valid, dpt_system_resource_invalid, dpt_system_resource_valid_with_dpti, dpt_system_resource_valid_without_dpti
Notes: PCIe exerciser VIP required
Exerciser PAL APIs Used: pal_exerciser_set_param (DMA_ATTRIBUTES, CFG_TXN_ATTRIBUTES); pal_exerciser_get_param (ATS_RES_ATTRIBUTES); pal_exerciser_ops (ATS_TXN_REQ, START_DMA, ATS_INV_CACHE)

Rule Description: Measured integrated TDISP devices may skip DPT checks but not GPC.
Coverage: dpt_system_resource_valid_without_dpti, dpt_system_resource_valid_with_dpti, dpt_system_resource_invalid, dpt_p2p_same_rootport_valid, dpt_p2p_same_rootport_invalid, dpt_p2p_different_rootport_valid, dpt_p2p_different_rootport_invalid
Notes: PCIe exerciser VIP required
Exerciser PAL APIs Used: pal_exerciser_set_param (DMA_ATTRIBUTES, CFG_TXN_ATTRIBUTES); pal_exerciser_get_param (ATS_RES_ATTRIBUTES); pal_exerciser_ops (ATS_TXN_REQ, START_DMA, ATS_INV_CACHE)

Rule Description: RME-DA coherent links attach only permitted coherent devices and cover attestation-relevant logic.
RME-CDA coherent devices support compliant TDI assignment, encryption, MEC, and coherency behavior.
A TDI in TDISP ERROR state poisons relevant Realm cached data and snoop responses.
A TDI entering CONFIG_UNLOCKED invalidates device-held TDI state, cache copies, and ATC entries.
Required coherent-device operations are unaffected by TDI state.
Security-sensitive RME-CDA device registers are DSM-controlled or DSM-verified before lock.
RME coherent devices protect Realm state on reset or power transitions.
A TDI entering CONFIG_UNLOCKED scrubs all associated DCM contents.
An access from a PE to any memory location, including to DCM, is subject to host-side GPC.
DCM access follows host-side GPC or device-side PAS checks based on PAS_CHECK.
An RME-CDA coherent device does not permit an internal access to DCM to specify Access PAS == Realm if the access is not from a TDI in the RUN TDISP state.
An RME-CDA coherent device does not permit an external access to DCM to specify Access PAS == Realm if the access did not arrive over an IDE Stream provisioned through TDISP.
Device-side PAS checks block speculative access to read-sensitive locations until complete.
If PAS_CHECK == TRUE, device-side PAS protection checks apply both to internal access and external access to DCM.
Hosts forward snoops to coherent devices only when the device is permitted to observe the location.
Host ports return poison/fixed data when blocked snoops might otherwise expose dirty device-owned data.
RME-CDA devices set CHI SEC_SID and RID correctly for TDI device-to-host requests.
RME-CDA device-to-host PAs are obtained through ATS or an equivalent host translation protocol.
An SMMU in an RME-CDA system supports populating the TE Memory Attribute bit (TE bit) in ATS Translation completions with the resolved PA space.
An RME-CDA coherent device guarantees that a TDI can generate device-to-host snoop requests only to PAs that it is allowed to directly access.
A host port must be able to identify that a PA of a device-to-host access falls within the DCM range of the coherent device attached to that port.
Host ports apply GPC and Realm DPT checks to relevant device-to-host PA requests.
Host ports check device-to-host Requester IDs against the permitted RID range.
Host ports apply DCM range handling for device-to-host snoop requests and skip GPC/DPT for them.
Devices handle blocked insecure snoops consistently with receiving poisoned snoop responses.
RME-CDA coherent devices must not send DVM CHI requests.
Notes: Requires CHI/C2C opcode trace visibility; ACS cannot prove absence from software.

Rule Description: Device-to-host traffic uses only MECIDs permitted for the device.
All structures and fields defined by this specification use little-endian convention.
MSD SMEM is in the Root PAS.
The address ranges of MSD SMEM are either defined statically or defined by SSD following an RME system reset.
Notes: MSD SMEM address definition is platform/SSD policy.

Rule Description: On an RME system reset MSD SMEM is either immediately assigned to the Root PAS or scrubbed and is available for access by the PE boot ROM as soon as it starts executing.
RMSD SMEM is in the Realm PAS.
The address ranges of SMEM assigned to the Realm PAS and Secure PAS are either defined statically or by SSD or MSD.
Notes: SMEM address definition is platform/SSD/MSD policy.

Rule Description: SMEM that can be dynamically assigned to the Realm PAS or the Secure PAS is either immediately assigned to the Root PAS or scrubbed on an RME system reset.
The access control path that protects SMEM is not affected by state from non-shielded memory.
Notes: SMEM protection path details are implementation-specific.

Rule Description: All A-profile application PEs in the system implement the Realm Management Extension (RME).
An SMMU in an RME system complies with SMMU for RME [3] and, if the system supports RME-DA or MEC, with SMMU for RME-DA.
In a system that supports RME-DA, any access from a TDISP-compliant device is subject to SMMU translation.
All bus and interconnect decoding components between the point where the Access PAS is assigned and the PoPA are PAS tag-aware.
Notes: Bus/interconnect PAS-awareness is covered indirectly by access behavior.

Rule Description: An RME coherent interconnect supports cache maintenance operations to the PoPA in compliance with the Arm A-profile architecture [1].
A PoPA CMO applies to any cache before the PoPA, including system caches that are located beyond the Point of Coherency.
Completion of a PoPA CMO cleans dirty state beyond PoPA and invalidates cached state before PoPA.
For any cache before the PoPA, cache prefetching across granule-boundary is allowed only after querying the GPC for the PAS association of the next granule.
Notes: Cache prefetch behavior is not directly software-observable.

Rule Description: A cache maintenance operation performed on a Clean cache entry never results with a write of entry content past the PoPA.
Notes: Clean-cache writeback behavior is not directly software-observable.

Rule Description: An RME coherent interconnect complies with a Distributed Virtual Memory (DVM) version that supports Realm Translation Regimes and TLB Invalidate by PA operations.
A PA of an access to a PCIe Root Port is associated with a PAS until reaching the Root Port.
Notes: PCIe exerciser VIP required

Rule Description: Interconnect registers that control mapping of PAs to PCIe Root Ports are implemented as MSD-Protected registers (MPRs).
RME-DA host bridge BDF, ECAM, and memory-range assignments are static or trusted-controlled.
Encryption keys or any other confidential memory encryption context that is used by an MPE are stored in registers that are reset to a known default value on an RME system reset.
Notes: MPE key storage is implementation-defined and not directly observable.

Rule Description: Any PAS other than the Non-secure PAS must have encryption enabled.
The decision to enable encryption for the Non-secure PAS is either hardwired or defined at boot and immutable once set.
An MPE integrity error is reported as an external abort to a software or hardware agent consuming the error.
Notes: MPE integrity error delivery depends on implementation-specific error injection.

Rule Description: Any captured details of an MPE integrity error are only visible to MSD.
Notes: MPE error capture visibility is implementation-specific.

Rule Description: An MPE property that is reported through the System Properties structure in Root Non-volatile Storage (RNVS) is supported for all external memory ports in the system.
Notes: RNVS-reported MPE properties are implementation-defined.

Rule Description: A Trusted SCP is an on-chip control processor that is trusted by MSD and can access resources in the Root PAS.
Notes: Trusted SCP may be non-A-profile trusted hardware.

Rule Description: A Trusted SCP is a Trusted subsystem and meets the applicable CCA security requirements.
Notes: Trusted SCP may be non-A-profile trusted hardware.

Rule Description: It is permitted for a Trusted SCP to have a mechanism to bypass a PAS filter that filters its transactions.
Notes: Trusted SCP may be non-A-profile trusted hardware.

Rule Description: An RME-DA RP sets the TEE-IO Supported bit in the Device Capabilities Register.
RME-DA Root Ports support the required Selective IDE Stream features.
An RME-DA RP exposes an IMPLEMENTATION DEFINED IDE key programming interface for the following IDE Key Management (IDE_KM) data objects:; KEY_PROG.; K_SET_GO.; K_SET_STOP.
Notes: IDE key programming interface is implementation-defined.

Rule Description: An RME-DA RP must support IDE key refresh operations in compliance with [4].
Notes: IDE key refresh requires implementation-specific software support.

Rule Description: RP IDE logic detects when an IDE key set requires refresh and either signals Trusted firmware or makes the stream Insecure.
Notes: IDE key refresh detection is implementation-defined and not software-observable.

Rule Description: RMSD ensures that Selective IDE Streams are configured such that different streams are assigned RID ranges and address ranges that do not overlap.
Notes: IDE stream range allocation is RMSD/RMM policy, not generic ACS behavior.

Rule Description: The RME-DA DVSEC implements the required PCIe register layout.
When TDISP is enabled, security-sensitive RP registers are RMSD write-protect.
When TDISP is enabled, IDE keys, confidential state, and protected payload registers are RMSD full-protect.
When TDISP is enabled, protected RP configuration registers are RMSD write-detect.
When RMEDA_CTL1.TDISP_EN transitions from 1 to 0, all hosted IDE Streams transition to IDE Insecure state.
When TDISP is disabled, Root Ports clear/reject protected T-bit or XT-bit traffic.
Notes: PCIe exerciser VIP required

Rule Description: The RMEDA_CTL registers are RMSD write-protect by hardware default.
All RPs in an RME-DA system must implement the RME-DA DVSEC.
Selective IDE register-block lock state controls register protection and stream lock state.
RME-DA Root Ports associate outgoing TLPs with IDE streams and set T-bit/XT-bit correctly.
Notes: PCIe exerciser VIP required

Rule Description: An RME-DA RP sets the IDE T-bit for an outgoing PCIe Memory Request or Configuration Request based on the request PAS.
Root Ports set the IDE T-bit on PCIe messages according to DTI, VDM, and message type.
Notes: PCIe message IDE T-bit requires packet visibility not available to ACS.

Rule Description: PCIe completions set IDE T-bit according to IDE and TDISP rules.
Notes: PCIe completion IDE T-bit is not software-observable in generic ACS.

Rule Description: Protected outgoing T-bit/XT-bit requests are rejected unless bound to a locked Secure IDE stream.
With TDISP enabled, Root Ports allow protected incoming T-bit/XT-bit requests only when permitted.
Notes: PCIe exerciser VIP required

Rule Description: Root Ports map incoming requests to SMMU SEC_SID, StreamID, and SubstreamID correctly.
Notes: PCIe exerciser VIP required

Rule Description: Root Complex P2P completions are returned only from the intended target peer.
Notes: PCIe exerciser VIP required

Rule Description: TDISP-enabled Root Port debug features are disabled unless explicitly authorized.
Notes: Root Port debug functionality is implementation-defined.

Rule Description: Security-affecting RP reset or state loss transitions hosted IDE streams to Insecure.
Requests that are autonomously initiated by the RP over its host interface are tagged with PAS == Non-secure.
Notes: PCIe exerciser VIP required

Rule Description: Root Ports poison affected TLPs or transition IDE streams to Insecure on integrity errors.
Notes: PCIe exerciser VIP required

Rule Description: An RME system must not include an SMMU that supports the XT extensions, unless all RPs either support the XT extensions or override the XT-bit to 0 for incoming requests.
TDISP XT-capable Root Ports set XT-bit behavior according to XT enablement and traffic type.
As a completer of memory requests, a TDISP-compliant RCiEP extracts the request IDE T-bit from the request PAS.
RCiEP requesters set SEC_SID, StreamID, and SubstreamID according to T-bit and requester identity.
Notes: PCIe exerciser VIP required

Rule Description: The PCIe segment and RIDs that are allocated to an RCiEP are either defined statically or configured using an RMSD write-protect register.
Notes: PCIe segment/RID ownership is static or RMSD-protected and not generically modifiable.

Rule Description: Exposed CTC coherent links support cryptographic encryption and integrity protection.
A coherent host port that supports RME-CDA implements the Coherent RME-DA DVSEC (RME-CDA DVSEC).
Coherent host-port system address ranges are controlled by HDM decoders or RMSD-protected registers.
The RME-CDA DVSEC implements the required PCIe register layout.
With CDA TDISP enabled, security-sensitive coherent host-port registers are RMSD write-protect.
With CDA TDISP enabled, IDE keys, confidential state, and protected payload registers are RMSD full-protect.
When RMECDA_CTL1.TDISP_EN transitions from 1 to 0, all IDE Streams transition to IDE Insecure state.
When CDA TDISP is disabled, Realm device/host memory requests are rejected.
Notes: CHI-C2C exerciser VIP required
Exerciser PAL APIs Used: pal_exerciser_set_param (CFG_TXN_ATTRIBUTES, EXERCISER_SEC_SID, DMA_ATTRIBUTES, EXERCISER_CXL_CMD_OP, EXERCISER_CXL_CMD_ADDR); pal_exerciser_get_param (EXERCISER_CXL_CMD_DATA0); pal_exerciser_ops (START_DMA, CXL_CMD_START)

Rule Description: The RMECDA_CTL registers are RMSD write-protect by hardware default.
All host ports in a system that supports Coherent RME-DA implement the RME-CDA DVSEC.
Coherent Link IDE lock state controls register protection and stream lock state.
Unlocked coherent link streams reject Realm host-to-device requests.
With CDA TDISP enabled, Realm device-to-host requests are permitted only on locked active links or equivalent safe paths.
Notes: CHI-C2C exerciser VIP required

Rule Description: Locked CDA host ports reject out-of-range or invalid Requester IDs.
Notes: CHI-C2C exerciser VIP required

Rule Description: In an RME system, if a Type-3 memory expansion device does not support target-side memory encryption then its memory must be encrypted by a host-side MPE.
Notes: CXL Type-3 endpoint required

Rule Description: A host-side MPE shall comply with initiator-based memory encryption requirements specified in CXL-TSP.
Notes: CXL Type-3 endpoint required

Rule Description: Exposed CXL memory-expansion links use CXL IDE link protection.
Notes: CXL Type-3 endpoint required

Rule Description: Type-3 CXL devices without CXL-TSP are allowed only when host-side protection conditions are met.
Notes: CXL Type-3 endpoint required

Rule Description: CXL Root Ports without active CDA TDISP tag back-invalidate snoops as Non-secure.
Notes: CXL exerciser VIP required

Rule Description: CMOs targeting CXL Type-3 memory reach all relevant host-side and device-side cache locations.
Notes: CXL exerciser VIP required

Rule Description: CXL Root Ports either support RME-CDA DVSEC or force/reject protected traffic safely.
Notes: CXL exerciser VIP required
Exerciser PAL APIs Used: pal_exerciser_set_param (CFG_TXN_ATTRIBUTES, DMA_ATTRIBUTES, EXERCISER_CXL_CMD_OP, EXERCISER_CXL_CMD_ADDR); pal_exerciser_get_param (EXERCISER_CXL_CMD_DATA0); pal_exerciser_ops (START_DMA, CXL_CMD_START)

Rule Description: If a CXL RP is not subject to GPC then CXL.cache must be disabled for it using an MSD-protected register.
A CXL Root Port that implements the RME-CDA DVSEC must comply with CXL-TSP.
CXL Root Ports map PAS and MECID to CXL TEE attributes and CKIDs correctly.
Notes: CXL Type-3 endpoint required

Rule Description: With CDA TDISP enabled, CXL Root Port and host bridge security registers are RMSD write-protect.
A programming interface that allows read and write access to RNVS must be in the Root PAS.
Notes: RNVS controls and reported properties are implementation-defined.

Rule Description: The system supports a method for permanently blocking write access from application PEs to all RNVS parameters.
The system supports a method for permanently blocking read access from application PEs to RNVS confidential parameters.
Notes: RNVS controls and reported properties are implementation-defined.

Rule Description: System support for any memory protection property reported in System Properties is immutable and applicable for all DRAM memory controllers in the system.
Notes: RNVS controls and reported properties are implementation-defined.

Rule Description: The memory-mapped registers of a Root watchdog are in the Root PAS.
A Root watchdog is capable of triggering an RME system reset when predefined expiration conditions are met.
MSD and RMSD are provided with a private interface for accessing a True Random Number Generator (TRNG) that meets the certification profile of the system.
Tenant-hosted HES is isolated from other tenants in the Trusted subsystem.
Notes: HES may be implemented in non-A-profile trusted hardware.

Rule Description: The HES implementation exposes a private interface to SSD components such as Trusted subsystems for requesting HES services.
Notes: HES may be implemented in non-A-profile trusted hardware.

Rule Description: The HES implementation exposes a programming interface in the Root PAS, shared by all application PEs, allowing MSD and PE Initial boot ROM to request for HES services.
Notes: HES may be implemented in non-A-profile trusted hardware.

Rule Description: HES has exclusive read and write access to RNVS confidential parameters.
Notes: HES may be implemented in non-A-profile trusted hardware.

Rule Description: A measurement register can be either extended using a secure hash algorithm, locked or reset.
Notes: HES may be implemented in non-A-profile trusted hardware.

Rule Description: HES has exclusive access to extend, lock, and reliably obtain the value of a measurement register it owns.
Notes: HES may be implemented in non-A-profile trusted hardware.

Rule Description: Once locked, a measurement cannot be further extended until it is reset.
Notes: HES may be implemented in non-A-profile trusted hardware.

Rule Description: An RME system reset is the only method to reset a measurement owned by HES.
Notes: HES may be implemented in non-A-profile trusted hardware.

Rule Description: On an RME system reset, HES state is reset to a known value, including all measurements and ephemeral cryptographic context.
Notes: HES may be implemented in non-A-profile trusted hardware.

Rule Description: A register that is located outside of the Root PAS but can affect a service provided by MSD must be implemented as a measurable register.
Notes: Measurable-register selection is implementation-defined.

Rule Description: A measurable register is a write-lockable register that MSD has a trusted method to obtain its value.
Notes: Measurable-register implementation is platform specific.

Rule Description: Only SSD or MSD are capable of controlling whether recording is performed for error records that might contain confidential information.
Notes: RAS/error injection behavior is outside generic ACS scope.

Rule Description: Critical Error Interrupts (CI) must be wired to a Trusted subsystem that will respond with an RME system reset.
Notes: RAS/error injection behavior is outside generic ACS scope.

Rule Description: An uncontainable error results in an RME system reset.
Notes: RAS/error injection behavior is outside generic ACS scope.

Rule Description: Only SSD or MSD can enable or disable Critical Error Interrupt generation.
Notes: RAS/error injection behavior is outside generic ACS scope.

Rule Description: Where an MPE provides support for integrity, if it detects an integrity error it can perform one of the following responses.
Notes: RAS/error injection behavior is outside generic ACS scope.

Rule Description: Only SSD or MSD must be able to control the abilities of detecting, propagating, and reporting MPE integrity errors.
Notes: RAS/error injection behavior is outside generic ACS scope.

Rule Description: MPEs pass poison information while preserving encryption and integrity behavior.
Notes: RAS/error injection behavior is outside generic ACS scope.

Rule Description: RME systems propagate MPAM_SP to all relevant MSCs.
Notes: MPAM MSC propagation is implementation/platform specific.

Rule Description: Allocation and protection of the address range assigned to an MTE carve-out are controlled by either SSD or MSD.
A system PMU counter that is accessible in the Secure PAS can only count events that are attributable to the Secure PAS or to the Non-secure PAS.
Notes: System PMU events and per-PAS controls are implementation-defined.

Rule Description: A system PMU counter that is accessible in the Realm PAS can only count events that are attributable to the Realm PAS or to the Non-secure PAS.
Notes: System PMU events and per-PAS controls are implementation-defined.

Rule Description: A system PMU counter that is accessible in the Root PAS can count events that are attributable to any PAS.
Notes: System PMU events and per-PAS controls are implementation-defined.

Rule Description: Non-secure-accessible PMU counters need per-PAS authorization to count PAS-specific events.
Notes: System PMU events and per-PAS controls are implementation-defined.

Rule Description: Per-PAS PMU authorization is driven by debug authentication or an appropriate PAS/Root register.
Notes: System PMU events and per-PAS controls are implementation-defined.

Rule Description: An event that is not explicitly associated with a PAS but can leak confidential information is implicitly associated with the Root PAS.
Notes: System PMU events and per-PAS controls are implementation-defined.

Rule Description: Application PEs in an RME system do not have architectural differences unless this is explicitly permitted by this specification.
Implementation-defined PE differences must not weaken the RME security guarantee.
Notes: Requires platform-specific review of implementation-defined PE properties.

Rule Description: PE behavior is unpredictable when visible implementation differences are mismatched across PEs.
Notes: UNPREDICTABLE mismatch conditions cannot be safely induced by generic ACS.

Rule Description: A software-initiated power state transition in an RME system at any level of the system hierarchy (PE, PE-cluster, System) is validated by MSD or by a Trusted subsystem.
Notes: Power-transition validation is platform/firmware policy.

Rule Description: Save/Restore operations for MSD PE context can only be done by MSD or a Trusted subsystem and use storage that is not accessible from Realm, Secure and Non-secure states.
Notes: MSD PE context save/restore path is firmware/platform specific.

Rule Description: Save/Restore operations for RMSD PE context can only be done by RMSD, MSD, or a Trusted subsystem and use storage that is not accessible from Secure and Non-secure states.
Notes: RMSD PE context save/restore path is firmware/platform specific.

Rule Description: Secure PE context save/restore uses authorized agents and storage hidden from Realm and Non-secure states.
Notes: Secure PE context save/restore path is firmware/platform specific.

Rule Description: Power-policy or hardware-mode registers are MPRs or otherwise SSD-constrained.
Notes: Power-policy registers are implementation-defined.

Rule Description: Any power management operation that can affect MSD state or the RME security guarantee must be validated by MSD or a Trusted subsystem.
Notes: Power-management validation is platform/firmware policy.

Rule Description: On an exit from a low power state in which system context is preserved, power control guarantees that MSD state is fully preserved.
Save/Restore operations for MSD state can only be done by MSD or a Trusted subsystem and use on-chip storage that is not accessible from Realm PAS, Secure PAS or Non-secure PAS.
An MPE or a PAS filter in a non-ACTIVE mode in which context is not fully retained blocks its operation and does not service requests until it is in ACTIVE mode again.
An MMU-attached PAS filter in a non-ACTIVE mode either continues to respond to GPT cache invalidations, or invalidates any cached state when moving back to ACTIVE mode.
Notes: PCIe exerciser VIP required

Rule Description: RMSD external debugging and Root external debugging are disabled by default on a Secured Arm CCA system.
Notes: External debug requires a common debugger/test interface unavailable to ACS.

Rule Description: RMSD external debugging can only be authorized following an RME system reset and before RMSD firmware is loaded and cannot change state until a subsequent RME system reset.
Notes: External debug requires a common debugger/test interface unavailable to ACS.

Rule Description: Root external debugging can only be authorized following an RME system reset and before MSD firmware is loaded and cannot change state until a subsequent RME system reset.
Notes: External debug requires a common debugger/test interface unavailable to ACS.

Rule Description: When Root external debugging is enabled, the RNVS confidential parameters are either inaccessible, scrubbed, or populated with debug values.
Notes: External debug requires a common debugger/test interface unavailable to ACS.

Rule Description: Access to a Secured Arm CCA system through an external debug or test interface, including debug access ports, JTAG ports, and scan interfaces is disabled by default.
Notes: External debug requires a common debugger/test interface unavailable to ACS.

Rule Description: External debug power-up requests are permitted only through trusted power control.
Notes: External debug requires a common debugger/test interface unavailable to ACS.

Rule Description: RME system reset resets Trusted requesters/subsystems and clears confidential state by trusted mechanisms.
Notes: Full trusted-state reset coverage is platform specific.

Rule Description: An RME system reset propagates to PEs as either a Cold reset, Warm reset, or Error recovery reset.
An RME system reset might propagate to any component that implements RAS [12] as an Error recovery reset.
Notes: RAS error-recovery reset propagation is implementation-specific.

Rule Description: The reset of a system component that affects the RME security guarantee can only be controlled by MSD or a Trusted subsystem, or driven by an RME system reset.
Notes: Security-affecting reset controls are implementation/platform specific.

Rule Description: LEGACY_TZ_EN is not permitted to change value after RME system reset has been deasserted.
A system that contains RME components, that have the LEGACY_TZ_EN input, will drive a common tie-off input value into all components.
If LEGACY_TZ_EN is TRUE, PAS[1] is driven to 0b0 by any logic that enforces Table
A PE that supports the LEGACY_TZ_EN tie-off hides the RME capability if LEGACY_TZ_EN is TRUE and reverts all functionality defined by RME.
A legacy completer is attached to an RME IP by driving the NS signal of the completer from PAS[0] of the RME IP.
Notes: Legacy requester/completer attachment is integration-specific.

Rule Description: A legacy requester is attached to an RME IP by driving PAS[0] of the RME IP from the NS signal of the legacy requester and driving PAS[1] of the RME IP to 0b0.
Notes: Legacy requester/completer attachment is integration-specific.

Rule Description: Multi-chip CTC interfaces transport PAS tags, MECIDs, CMOs, and DVM messages as required.
Notes: Multi-chip CTC transport is platform specific.

Rule Description: If an RME system supports 4 MPAM PARTID spaces, the CTC interface transports the MPAM_SP[1:0] indication.
Notes: MPAM/CTC multi-chip signaling is implementation/platform specific.

Rule Description: An RME system reset in a multi-chip system affects all nodes.
Notes: Multi-chip CTC reset behavior is platform specific.

Rule Description: Physically exposed CTC interfaces support cryptographic link encryption and integrity protection.
Notes: CTC link protection needs platform/fabric visibility outside generic ACS.

Rule Description: CTC link protection provides IDE-equivalent or stronger encryption and integrity.
Notes: CTC link-protection strength needs platform/fabric visibility outside generic ACS.
